questions.q: The magnetic field B crossing normally a square metallic plate of area 4 m2 is changing with time as shown in figure. The magnitude of induced emf in the plate during t=2 s to t=4 s, is _____ mV.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the graph, it can be seen that the value of the magnetic field at t=2 s is 4 mT, whereas the magnetic field at t=4 s is 8 mT.

The formula to calculate the magnitude of the induced emf is given by

εind =dϕdt=ddtBA=AdBdt   ...1

dBdt is the slope of the given graph.

Hence, the value of the induced emf can be calculated as follows:

εind =4 m2×8 mT-4 mT4 s-2 s=8 mV

questions.q: A horizontal straight wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> long extending from east to west falling freely at right angle to horizontal component of earth's magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Wb</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The instantaneous value of emf induced in the wire when its velocity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Horizontal component of earth's magnetic field, 

BH=0.60×10-4 Wb m-2.

Induced emf e=BHvℓ

=0.60×10-4×10×5

=3×10-3 V

questions.q: A circular coil of 1000 turns each with area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is rotated about its vertical diameter at the rate of one revolution per second in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>07</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The maximum voltage generation will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, N=1000, A=1 m2 and B=0.07 T

The maximum emf generated is εmax=NBAω,

=NBA2πf

 =1000×0.07×1×2π1=140π

Thus, maximum emf is 439.6 V≈440 V.

questions.q: The current in an inductor is given by $\mathrm{I}=(3 \mathrm{t}+8)$ where $\mathrm{t}$ is in second. The magnitude of induced emf produced in the inductor is $12 \mathrm{mV}$. The self-inductance of the inductor _____ $\mathrm{mH}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=3 \mathrm{t}+8 \\ & \varepsilon=12 \mathrm{mV} \\ & |\varepsilon|=\mathrm{L}\left|\frac{\mathrm{dI}}{\mathrm{dt}}\right| \\ & 12=\mathrm{L} \times 3 \\ & \mathrm{~L}=4 \mathrm{mH}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Three identical resistors with resistance R=12 Ω and two identical inductors with sell inductance L=5 mH are connected to an ideal battery with emf of 12 V as shown in figure. The current through the battery long after the switch has been closed will be________A.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that after long time an inductor offers zero resistance i.e., in steady state condition.

Here all three identical resistors are in parallel, so equivalent resistance is, Req=123=4 Ω

Now, current through the battery is I=124=3 A

questions.q: A coil has an inductance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> and resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is applied across the coil. The energy stored in the magnetic field after the current has built up to its equilibrium value will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The data given is 

L=2 HR=4 ΩV=10 V

Using Ohm's law, V=IR,

 I=10 V4 Ω=52 A

The energy of an inductor is given by 
    E=12LI2=12×2×254=625×10-2 J

questions.q:
A circular conducting coil of radius 1 m is being heated by the change of magnetic field B→ passing perpendicular to the plane in which the coil is laid. The resistance of the coil is 2 μΩ. The magnetic field is slowly switched off such that its magnitude changes in time as

B=4π×10-3 T1-t100

The energy dissipated by the coil before the magnetic field is switched off completely is E=______mJ.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
ϕ=B→·S→

ϕ=4π×10-31-t100·πR2

ϕ=4×10-3×121-t100

ε=-dϕdt

ε=-ddt4×10-31-t100

ε=4×10-31100=4×10-5 V

When B=0

1-t100=0

t=100 sec

Heat =ε2Rt

Heat =4×10-522×10-6×100 J

Heat =16×10-10×1002×10-6 J

Heat =0.08 J

Heat =80 mJ

questions.q: A conducting bar moves on two conducting rails as shown in the figure. A constant magnetic field B exists into the page. The bar starts to move from the vertex at time $t=0$ with a constant velocity. If the induced EMF is $\mathrm{E} \propto \mathrm{t}^{\mathrm{n}}$, then value of n is _.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the bar moves without change in orientation, the length of bar will be proportional to its distance from the vertex.
i.e. $I=c(v t)\begin{aligned}
& \text { induced emf } E=B / v \\
& =c B v^2 t
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow n=1$

questions.q: Two coils have mutual inductance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>002</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math>. The current changes in the first coil according to the relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mi>π</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The maximum value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>emf</mi></math> in the second coil is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi>α</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The amount of flux induced in the second coil due to the first one is given by

ϕ2=Mi=Mi0sinωt   ...1

where, M is the mutual inductance of the coils.

The formula to calculate the emf induced can be written as

ε=-dϕ2dt   ...2

From equation (2), it follows that,

εmax=Mi0ω=0.002×5×50π V=π2 V

Hence, α=2.

questions.q:
A square shaped coil of area 70 cm2 having 600 turns rotates in a magnetic field of 0.4 Wb m–2, about an axis which is parallel to one of the side of the coil and perpendicular to the direction of field. If the coil completes 500 revolution in a minute, the instantaneous emf when the plane of the coil is inclined at 60° with the field, will be ______ V.

(Take π=227)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, N=600, A=70×10-4 m2, and B=0.4 T

Angular speed of coil is ω=2πn60=500×2π60=100π6 rad s-1

Instantaneous emf in coil is given by ε=-Ndϕdt, where, magnetic flux ϕ=BAcosωt and ωt=30° is angle between A and B.

So, ε=-NdBAcosωtdt=-N-BAωsinωt=NBAωsinωt

Putting the values, we get

ε=600×70×10-4×0.4×100π6×12

=44 V

questions.q: In the given figure, an inductor and resistor are connected in series with a battery of emf E volt. Ea2b J s-1 represents the maximum rate at which the energy is stored in the magnetic field (inductor). The numerical value of ba will be _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the current flowing through an L-R circuit is given by

i=ER1-e-RtL   ...1

The energy stored within the inductor can be calculated as follows:

Einduction =12Li2=12LE2R21-e-RtL2   ...2

The rate of change of energy stored within the inductor is given by

ddtEinduction =21-e-RtL·e-RtL·RL·E2L2R2=E2Re-RtL-e-2RtL   ...3

For maximum rate,

d2Edt2=0   ...4

From equation (3) and (4), it can be written that

ddtE2Re-RtL-e-2RtL =0⇒e-RtL=2e-2RtL  ⇒eRtL=2   ...5

From equation (3) and (5), it can be written, under maximum energy stored condition for the circuit, that

ddtEinduction =E2R2-1-2-2=E24R

Substitute the values of the resistance and compare with the given expression to obtain the values of the parameters.

a=2b=2R=50

Hence, the required ratio is given by

ba=25

questions.q: As per the given figure, if dIdt=-1 A s-1, then the value of VAB at this instant will be ______ V.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, dIdt=-1 A s-1

Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law to the circuit,

VA-IR-LdIdt-12=VB

⇒VA-2×12-6(-1)-12=VB

⇒VAB=VA-VB=36-6=30 V

The emf induced in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mfenced><mrow><mi>in</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mV</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> at the instant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>s is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ..........

questions.q: A square loop PQRS having 10 turns, area $3.6 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2$ and resistance $100 \Omega$ is slowly and uniformly being pulled out of a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $\mathrm{B}=0.5 \mathrm{~T}$ as shown. Work done in pulling the loop out of the field in $1.0 \mathrm{~s}$ is ______ $\times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \epsilon=N B \ell v \\ & i=\frac{\epsilon}{R}=\frac{N B \ell v}{R} \\ & F=N(i \ell B)=\frac{N^2 B^2 \ell^2 v}{R}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}=\mathrm{F} \times \ell=\frac{\mathrm{N}^2 \mathrm{~B}^2 \ell^3}{\mathrm{R}}\left(\frac{\ell}{\mathrm{t}}\right) \\ & \mathrm{A}=\ell^2 \\ & \mathrm{~W}=\frac{(10 \times 10)(0.5)^2 \times\left(3.6 \times 10^{-3}\right)^2}{100 \times 1} \\ & \mathrm{~W}=3.24 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: When a coil is connected across a $20 \mathrm{~V}$ dc supply, it draws a current of $5 \mathrm{~A}$. When it is connected across $20 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}$ ac supply, it draws a current of $4 \mathrm{~A}$. The self inductance of the coil is ______ $\mathrm{mH}$. $($ Take $\pi=3$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Case-I:
$i=\frac{20}{R} \Rightarrow R=4 \Omega$ Case-II:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{i}=\frac{20}{\mathrm{Z}} \\ & 4=\frac{20}{\sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{\mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2}=5 \\ & \mathrm{R}^2+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}^2=25 \Rightarrow \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}=3 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{L}=\frac{3}{2 \pi \mathrm{f}}=\frac{1}{2 \times 50}=\frac{1000}{100} \mathrm{mH} \\ & \mathrm{L}=10 \mathrm{mH}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A circular coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is placed in a uniform magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> with its plane perpendicular to the field initially. It is rotated at constant angular speed about an axis along the diameter of coil and perpendicular to magnetic field so that it undergoes half of rotation in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The maximum value of EMF induced (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>μV</mi></math>) in the coil will be close to the integer....
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Flux as a function of time ϕ=B→·A→=ABcos(ωt)

Emf induced,

e=-dϕdt=ABωsin(ωt)

Max. value of Emf = ABω

=πR2Bω

=3.14×0.1×0.1×3×10-5×π0.2=15

questions.q: A circular coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> turns is rotated about its vertical diameter with an angular speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The maximum emf induced in the coil will be _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> volt (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Emf=BωNAsinωt

Emfmax=BωNA=BωNπR2

=3×10-2×50×20×π×64104≈60×10-2 V

questions.q: A small square loop of wire of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>l</mi></math> is placed inside a large square loop of wire of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>l</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>. The loops are coplanar and their centers coincide. The value of the mutual inductance of the system is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo></math>______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Flux linkage for inner loop

ϕ=Bcenter×l2

=4×μ0i4πL2sin45°+sin45°l2

⇒ϕ=22μ0iπLl2

Therefore, mutual inductance will be

M=ϕi=22μ0l2πL=22μ0π

=224ππ×10-7

=82×10-7

=128×10-7 H

Hence, x=128.

questions.q: Magnetic flux (in weber) in a closed circuit of resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> varies with time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mfenced><mi>s</mi></mfenced></math> as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The magnitude of the induced current at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mA</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that magnetic flux ϕ=8t2-9t+5

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction

emf=-dϕdt=-16t-9

At t=0.25 s

emf=-16×0.25-9=5 V

Current =emf  Resistance =5 V20 Ω

=14 A=10004 mA=250 mA

questions.q: Conductor wire ABCDE with each $\operatorname{arm} 10 \mathrm{~cm}$ in length is placed in magnetic field of $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ Tesla, perpendicular to its plane. When conductor is pulled towards right with constant velocity of $10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$, induced emf between points A and E is _____ mV.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As field is uniform we can replace the bent wire with straight wire from $A$ to $B$.
So EMF :
$\varepsilon=\mathrm{Bv} \ell_{\mathrm{AB}}$
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{10 \mathrm{~cm}}{5} \times 2\left(10 \sin 45^{\circ}\right) \mathrm{cm} \\ & \varepsilon=10 \mathrm{mV}\end{aligned}$
